# javaabu/manifest

> Ships CSS, Sass, JS, TypeScript, React and Vue from Laravel packages to apps. Packages register assets in their service provider; Blade components declare what they need and it's injected into the page (or placed with @manifestStyles / @manifestScripts); the app's Vite builds everything through a plugin; Inertia renders package pages as package::Page; apps override any single file in resources/vendor/{package}.

Paths are relative to this file. In an app, that's vendor/javaabu/manifest/.

## Rules

- Assets are named `package::name`. Register them with `$this->registerAssets('pkg', __DIR__ . '/../resources', fn (Package $package) => ...)` (trait `Javaabu\Manifest\Concerns\RegistersAssets`), entries relative to the package's resources folder.
- A Blade component declares its assets with `#[RequiresAssets('pkg::asset')]` or `DeclaresAssets::requiredAssets()`; anonymous components and views use `@manifestRequire('pkg::asset')`. Don't add `<script>` or `<link>` tags for package assets by hand, and don't add package entries to the app's `laravel({ input })`.
- Required assets are injected automatically into HTML responses. Use `@manifestStyles` / `@manifestScripts` only to choose where they go.
- Order comes from `depends_on`. A script that needs its own CSS imports it (`import './select.css'`).
- Package JS is imported as `@javaabu/{name}` (after `->js()`), resolved by the Vite plugin: `import manifest from "./vendor/javaabu/manifest/dist/vite.js"` next to `laravel()`. Never copy package JS into the app to use it.
- Inertia: `Inertia::render('pkg::Page')`, and in the app `resolve: (name) => resolvePage(name, import.meta.glob("./pages/**/*.tsx"))` from `@javaabu/manifest/inertia`.
- To change a package's file, override that one file at `resources/vendor/{package}/<same path>` (`php artisan manifest:override pkg path`). Don't edit vendor/.
- Packages declare npm packages their code imports with `->npm()` (`for: 'pages'` for what only Inertia pages and alias imports need); apps run `php artisan manifest:check` to install them. Blade apps aren't asked for pages-only packages.
- Run `php artisan manifest:types` after installing packages in a TypeScript app.
- In tests, `Manifest::fake()` then `Manifest::assertAssetRequired('pkg::asset')`.
- Asset tags are rendered by Laravel's Vite: `Vite::useCspNonce()` and friends apply.
